title: New Jersey AI Laws

reading.body:
New Jersey has enacted one AI-related law, A3497, which targets algorithmic rent coordination rather than AI development or deployment.

The law amends the New Jersey Antitrust Act to reach coordinators, the software intermediaries that perform coordinating functions among rental property owners. It prohibits owners from using such coordinators, prohibits coordinators from facilitating agreements that restrict competition, prohibits parallel pricing coordination by two or more persons, and prohibits anyone from performing a coordinating function at all. The Attorney General must establish a complaint location and may write rules.

This is a pricing-conduct statute, not a compute or data center statute. It does not govern how AI systems are built, where they are sited, or how much power they draw. Its relevance to AI is that the prohibited conduct runs through software: the law defines algorithmic device and competitively sensitive information, which means enforcement will turn on what a pricing tool does with landlord data rather than on any single landlord's intent.

One law is a thin basis for a pattern. The data covers only enacted text, so it says nothing about bills that failed, pending proposals, or how aggressively the Attorney General will enforce. It also does not establish whether other states have taken the same approach, so no national trend can be read from it.

New Jersey has enacted 1 AI-related law. Each is read from its enrolled text: what it does, who it applies to, when it takes effect, and what it requires.

Enacted AI laws in New Jersey

1 law this site judged relevant to AI, newest first, each read from its enrolled text.

  • A3497: Establishes "Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act." passed 2026-07-20

    The act makes it unlawful and a violation of the New Jersey Antitrust Act for rental property owners to use coordinators that perform coordinating functions, for coordinators to facilitate agreements among rental property owners that restrict competition, for two or more persons to engage in parallel pricing coordination, and for any person to perform a coordinating function. It defines key terms such as algorithmic device, coordinating function, and competitively sensitive information. It requires the Attorney General to establish a complaint location and authorizes rulemaking.

How this page is kept

This page is generated from the enacted laws this site tracks for New Jersey. When the legislature passes another AI-related bill, it appears here the night the bill's text is read. The full 50-state picture is at State AI Laws.
